newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico replaces coffee trees in Guerrero state.
newsitem.headline: Mexico replaces coffee trees in Guerrero state.

text.p: Mexico's south-western state of Guerrero plans this year to continue to replace coffee trees on 2,500 hectares of prime growing zones, the Agriculture Ministry said Wednesday.

Guerrero Agriculture Ministry delegate Joel Duenas Rodriguez said the state would produce 13.4 million trees this year and plant them on the earmarked land where coffee trees have been deemed old and unproductive.
Last year, the state grew and planted 6.25 million coffee trees in the replacement program.
Duenas gave no indication of future production levels in the state stemming from the program, which this year will cost 8.8 million pesos.
Coffee grows on 50,773 hectares in Guerrero, one of Mexico's second-string growing states with 10,589 producers, according to Agriculture Ministry figures.

In the recently ended 1996-1997 cycle, Guerrero produced 231,020 60-kg bags of coffee compared to 228,090 bags in the 1995-1996 cycle, the Mexican Coffee Council said in a state-by-state breakdown of output.

Farm authorities have also handed out 600 manual depulping machines in Guerrero's growing zones of Costa Chica, Montana, and Costa Grande, and have also promoted the construction of drying patios, Duenas said.
